The *Soceyya Sutta* ("Purity", Iti 66; It 3.17, PTS It 55) is a discourse in the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta expounds three kinds of purity or cleanliness (*soceyya*): bodily purity, verbal purity, and mental purity [SuttaCentral]. Text-critical analysis of the collection's metrical summaries notes that the uddāna résumé reflects minor grammatical variations against the prose, utilizing simple adjective forms rather than the abstract noun *soceyya* [Moore 1908].

Scholars have examined the relationship between the verses of Iti 66 (alongside Iti 67) and the *Tikanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, noting that discourses such as AN 3.118–120 likely presuppose or quote these verses when distinguishing *soceyya* (comprising good conduct) from *moneyya* (associated with the state of an arahant), though the conceptual definitions do not require a prolonged doctrinal development [Bechert 1992]. SuttaCentral records the *Dutiyasoceyyasutta* (AN 3.121) as a direct passage-level parallel [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus likewise identifies significant Pali-internal text reuse with the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), sharing segments (§2.1–2.4) with AN 3.120 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records substantial internal formulaic parallels with neighboring *Itivuttaka* discourses—most prominently the *Moneyya Sutta* (Iti 67, sharing §0.1–4.1), the *Duccarita Sutta* (Iti 64), the *Cakkhu Sutta* (Iti 61), and the *Indriya Sutta* (Iti 62)—as well as the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus aligns Iti 66 automatically with passages in the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125, fascicle 12) [DharmaNexus].
